[April 2016]

Work has today begun on a 250m long fence spanning the Brenner Pass along the border between Austria and Italy. This is in anticipation of the expected influx of migrants, after the closure of the so-called 'Balkan route' earlier this year. The wall will stretch the length of the pass and will cover the motorway and the main road. In addition to the structure, a registration centre will be built on the Austrian side of the border.Traffic checks are expected to be in place as early as the beginning of May.

Austria's Interior Minister, Johanna Mikl-Leitner, met with her Italian counterpart in Rome last week to discuss the new border. The two agreed that the two countries will be co-operating in the near future to enforce Schengen principles. However, Gianni Pitella, president of the Progressive Alliance of Socialists and Democrats, was critical of the construction of the border. The president of the second largest party in the European Parliament stated that it was a clear violation of Schengen rules, and that it was more about 'national groups' rather than working towards the common goal for Europe.
